answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 56 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the beacon hash is checked against the oasis checkpoint at intake, the raven audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
